newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty lashes governments on refugee policies.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty lashes governments on refugee policies.

text.p: Amnesty International accused governments around the world on Wednesday of deliberately putting up barriers that keep even genuine refugees out of their countries.

"While the number of people needing international protection continues to grow, governments seems more concerned with keeping refugees away from their borders," the London-based human rights organisation said in a report.

"The new battery of techniques aimed at keeping refugees at bay mean that countless people never get a real chance to escape from torture or death threats, or are being sent back to countries where they run a real risk of getting thrown into jail or handed over to executioners," Amnesty said.
Amnesty said there were more than 15 million refugees worldwide and the numbers of people fleeing their homes was likely to grow in coming years, as demonstrated by the crisis in Albania.
It said that at this stage Italian authorities appeared to be admitting Albanian asylum-seekers and it urged all governments to fulfill their obligations towards them.
Amnesty criticised governments for applying asylum criteria harshly, detaining asylum seekers and fining airlines and shipping companies if they carry people without valid travel documents.

It cited the case of thousands of Haitian refugees who took to boats after the military coup in 1991. "In 1992, the United States intercepted Haitian boat people at sea and summarily returned them, without any examination of their claims," the report said.
Amnesty also cited the case of a Zairian woman who escaped from a military prison and sought asylum in Sweden claiming torture.

Amnesty said Swedish authorities rejected her claim on several grounds, including the view that the president does not control the military and therefore torture by soldiers does not constitute state persecution.
"While governments may have the right to control their borders, they do not have the right to refuse people access to asylum procedures," Amnesty said.
"The increasingly restrictive approach that more and more governments take towards refugees makes a mockery of their international and national obligations," it said.
